main_text.p: cori ratio habeatur: diligenter considerate quid cuiusque hominis status, sexus, aetas, dignitas, dona & munus postulent & ferant. Quid singularum actionum tum naturae tum praesentibus circumstantijs maxime conveniat. Atque ita omnia agite decenter & secundum ordinem, omnia recte agantur sine ulla rerum confusione, perturbatione & tumultu. Hic enim ordo taxis vel akatastasia opponitur.

Several words are blurred and uncertain: "ita omnia" and "1.omnia" in the line "cundum ordinem 1.omnia" are doubtful, and the Greek words "τάξις" and "ἀκαταστασία" are only approximately legible and are given in transliteration here; the original Greek is not reliably readable.
